knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Partial Derivative at a Point

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x, y) =2 y^{2} \tan{(x )}+\frac{y}{x}$, evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(\pi,2)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 y^{2} \tan{(x )}+\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 y^{2} \tan{(x )})+\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =2 y^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\tan{(x )})+y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =2 y^{2}\cdot (\sec^{2}{(x )})+y\cdot (- \frac{1}{x^{2}}) \\  & =2 y^{2} \sec^{2}{(x )}-\frac{y}{x^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(\pi,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(\pi,2)} & =2 (2)^{2} \sec^{2}{((\pi) )}-\frac{(2)}{(\pi)^{2}} \\  & =8-(\frac{2}{\pi^{2}}) \\  & =8 - \frac{2}{\pi^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3 y^{3} \ln{(x )}-2 \sqrt{y} x) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3 y^{3} \ln{(x )})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2 \sqrt{y} x) \\  & =3 \ln{(x )}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{3})-2 x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{y}) \\  & =3 \ln{(x )}\cdot (3 y^{2})-2 x\cdot (\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{y}}) \\  & =9 y^{2} \ln{(x )}-\frac{x}{\sqrt{y}}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3 x^{3} \cot{(y )}-y^{2} x^{2}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3 x^{3} \cot{(y )})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{2} x^{2}) \\  & =3 x^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\cot{(y )})-x^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{2}) \\  & =3 x^{3}\cdot (- \csc^{2}{(y )})-x^{2}\cdot (2 y) \\  & =- 3 x^{3} \csc^{2}{(y )}-2 y x^{2}\end{aligned}
